messages.subject: RecordTableIndividual CamtrapR question
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have been using the CamtrapR package for preparing the data for spatial capture-recapture models.

In my dataset, I have multiple pictures with more than one dingo identified. If for example, a picture contains dingo A and dingo B, I would expect that the Record Table should include a line for both dingoes, unless these dingoes were found in another picture less than the minDeltaTime specified. However, I have realised that the resulting Record Table would only take into consideration the first individual recorded (Dingo A) in the ‘HierarchicalSubject’ of the metadata of each picture and not the subsequent identified individuals (Dingo B, C, etc).

Here is the code I have been using:

recordTableIndividualDingo <- recordTableIndividual(inDir  = wd_images_ID_dingoes,

IDfrom                 = "metadata",

hasStationFolders      = FALSE,         # images are not in station directories

metadataIDTag          = "Individual_dingo",

additionalMetadataTags =  c("EXIF:AmbientTemperature", "UserLabel",  "EXIF:Model"),

minDeltaTime           = 10,

deltaTimeComparedTo    = "lastIndependentRecord",

metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|")

A quick way that I found to work around this problem was to add the argument ‘removeDuplicateRecords = FALSE’ in the function recordTableIndividual.

The resulting table seems to include all individuals in the pictures (e.g. Dingo A AND Dingo B). I would then remove the ‘real’ duplicates from the table (that is the lines containing the same individual during the exact same time) as so:

recordTableIndividual_final <-recordTableIndividual[!duplicated(recordTableIndividual[,c("Individual","DateTimeOriginal")]),]

This approach seems to give the correct results in the table.

If needed, I can share a subsample of the data extracted with exiftool. In the hierarchicalsubject column, we can find, for example:

Individual_dingo|DingoA, Individual_dingo|DingoB, SPECIES|Dog

I was wondering if anybody had any comments or suggestions about this specific situation.

Thank you very much in advance for your help,

Vanessa

messages.subject: Re: RecordTableIndividual CamtrapR question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vanessa,
thank you for the question. There is indeed a bug in the current code of recordTableIndividual.

As you described, the problem is this: if there are 2 or more individuals at the same station at the same time (i.e., you tagged different individuals in the same picture), and removeDuplicateRecords = TRUE, only one record will be returned (the first one) and the rest omitted. This may happen with both methods for individual ID: metadata tags and directories for individuals.

Please find attached 2 R scripts in which the problem should be fixed. They contain an updated version of recordTableIndividual and some helper functions needed by recordTableIndividual internally.

Can you please run/source both scripts (no need to change anything inside) and then rerun your recordTableIndividual code? Then please, let us know if it worked. If so, it will be part of the next camtrapR release.

Thank you very much for reporting.
Best,
Jürgen

Hi Elsa,
did you rename the tag groups in digiKam? In the metadata I see the relevant species tag as:

06Species|Chiroptera sp.

So when you run any function that extracts metadata the following will not work:
metadataSpeciesTag         = "Species"

Unfortunately I cannot test with the attached picture, as the metadata were removed during upload (likely a Google Group issue).

So maybe you renamed the tag group and did not update the tags in the images? The relevant button is called "Write metadata to each file"? messages.subject: Multi-session capthist question
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jürgen,

I am trying to create a multi-session capthist for my camera-trap study, which will be used in the SECR package for mark-resight analysis. In my study, I have 4 sessions; each with 17, 15, 15 and 15 occasions, respectively. While reading the CamtrapR manual, I did not find the option to take into consideration multiple sessions, other than by adding the argument ‘SessionCol’ in the SpatialDetectionHistory function.

So far, I ran the RecordTableIndividual function and added a column called ‘SessionCol’ in this record table. Based on the date of capture for each record, I attributed the corresponding session number (1, 2, 3 or 4). I ran the SpatialDetectionHistory function using this data, with the SessionCol argument. I realize that the resulting capthist object contains all 62 occasions (of the entire dataset) for each session. In other words, the ‘Usage range by occasion’ and the ‘Counts by occasion’ for each session spans from Occasion 1 to 62 (But for, for example, Session 1 has no detections between occasions 18 and 62).

Also, the resulting SDH table contains occasion IDs ranging between 1-62 rather than 1-17 for Session 1, 1-15 for Session 2, etc. It seems to me that this will cause problems when using the read.capthist function of the SECR package, since the occasion IDs are not separated per session. (If I understand correctly)

I also realised that the occasions were divided by occasion length throughout the entire data period, regardless of the time period for each session. For example, say that the occasion length is specified to 10 days, but Session 1 spans from day 1 to day 98: From what I can see, when using the function spatialdetectionhistory, day 99 and day 100 would be included in the 10th occasion (along with days 91 to 98) and, consequently, the 10th occasion would be split between Session 1 and Session 2.

I was wondering if I missed a step in my approach, or if there was a different way to separate the sessions with CamtrapR (Other than creating a camera operation matrix and SDH for each session separately). I am happy to provide further information, if needed.

Thank you very much in advance,

Vanessa

messages.subject: Re: Multi-session capthist question
messages.body_plain:
You have 2 possibilities to define sessions in spatialDetectionHistory() by adding a sessionCol in:

1) recordTable (which you chose)
2) camera trap table.

Option 1 is for situations in which cameras were run continuously and you wish to cut that period into sessions. Option 2 is suitable if you used different cameras between sessions or if cameras were moved between sessions.

Which situation are you in?

You could try adding a sessionCol in the camera trap table (the equivalent of data(camtraps)). It would require duplicating the entries for the different sessions and adapting the setup/retrieval dates. I don't know if that will solve the issue and haven't tested it yet.

You could try with a sample data set and also send it to me (or share here) if you wish to. I don't have a multi-session data set to test with at the moment. It would be easier for me to check with a sample data set.

Best,
Jürgen

·         a station with 2 cameras would result in the value 4 if both cameras were active in both sessions

Error in spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableIndividualDingo,  :

  there is a mismatch between station IDs in CTtable and rownames in camOp

  In addition: Warning messages:

  1: In `!=.default`(CTtable[, stationCol], rownames(camOp)) :

   longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

  2: In is.na <http://is.na>(e1) | is.na <http://is.na>(e2):

    longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

The number of rows in camOp is equal to the number of stations. The number of rows in CTtable is equal to the total number of cameras running for each session. Before introducing the multi-session component to my analysis, I would delete the duplicated line in CTtable (that is if a station had 2 non-independent cameras, I would delete the line with the second camera and use the center point between both cameras as the GPS point for that station) in order to avoid this error message. However, when using multi-session data, the number of lines needs to be superior to the number of stations in order to keep the information on the sessions.

I could send you a subsample of my data for you to take a look, if you wish. Please let me know to which email address I should send my data.

Thank you very much again for your help,

Vanessa

messages.subject: Re: Multi-session capthist question
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vanessa,
I think it should work now. Please run both attached scripts and then just run spatialDetectionHistory on your native input tables. CTtable needs a session column, recordTable not.
The function will assign sessions to the records based on the session dates in CTtable.
Please note that you need to prepare the camera operation table by treating the sessions as cameras (see code below). This is just a workaround and not ideal, but should work as long as you don't have multiple cameras AND multiple sessions per station.

Based on the code and data you sent me, try the code below. It seems to work for me.

Note the following though:
- the number of stations differes between sessions (station 18 was not set up in session 2 in your data)
- argument "occasionStartTime" should be set to 0 (records may end up in wrong sessions if it is not 0 and records are close to the break between sessions)

- The first occasion of session 2 has only 1 day. The last occasion of session 1 has 5 days (at an occasion length of 6 and with day1 = “survey”). This is because of day1 = "survey"

Regarding your other questions:

> Also, the resulting SDH table contains occasion IDs ranging between 1-62 rather than 1-17 for Session 1, 1-15 for Session 2, etc. It seems to me that this will cause problems when using the read.capthist function of the SECR package, since the occasion IDs are not separated per session. (If I understand correctly)

Depends on argument day1. If day1 = "survey", it is numbered consecutively throughout the sessions (sessios 2 has occasion 16-32 for example). If day1 = "station", the numbers start at 1 in each session

> I also realised that the occasions were divided by occasion length throughout the entire data period, regardless of the time period for each session. For example, say that the occasion length is specified to 10 days, but Session 1 spans from day 1 to day 98: From what I can see, when using the function spatialdetectionhistory, day 99 and day 100 would be included in the 10th occasion (along with days 91 to 98) and, consequently, the 10th occasion would be split between Session 1 and Session 2.

I need to think about this. If a record is in day 99 and your second session begins on day 99, it should be included in session 2. Records in day 99 and 100 should not be included in session1. When an occasion is split between 2 sessions, this should be reflected in the effort matrix. If you don't mind, can you test this please and report?

Please give it a try and also play around with the arguments (day1 = “station”).

I’d be happy to hear from you if it worked or if you encountered any problems.

Thank you!

Jürgen

wd_tables <- "C:/BLA/BLA"   # set the directory containing your tables

camtraps_cam_S<-read.table(file.path(wd_tables, "Camtraps_cam_subsample_sessions.csv"),
                           header=T, sep=",", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# format dates
camtraps_cam_S$Setup_date <- as.Date(camtraps_cam_S$Setup_date)
camtraps_cam_S$Retrieval_date <- as.Date(camtraps_cam_S$Retrieval_date)
camtraps_cam_S$Problem1_from <- as.Date(camtraps_cam_S$Problem1_from, optional = F, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
camtraps_cam_S$Problem1_to <- as.Date(camtraps_cam_S$Problem1_to, optional = F, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
camtraps_cam_stations_only_S <-camtraps_cam_S[!duplicated(camtraps_cam_S[,c("Station", "Sessioncol")]),]

camop_session2 <- cameraOperation(CTtable      = camtraps_cam_stations_only_S,

                                 stationCol   = "Station",
                                 setupCol     = "Setup_date",
                                 retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
                                 writecsv     = FALSE,
                                 dateFormat   = "%Y-%m-%d",
                                 allCamsOn    = FALSE,

                                 cameraCol    = "Sessioncol",
                                 byCamera    = TRUE,
                                 camerasIndependent = TRUE,
                                 hasProblems  = TRUE
)
camopPlot(camop_session2)

recordTableIndividualDingo <- read.csv(file.path(wd_tables, "recordTableIndividualDingo_subsample.csv"),
                                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

sdh3 <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableIndividualDingo,
                                species               = "Identified_dingo_subsample",
                                camOp = camop_session2,
                                CTtable               = camtraps_cam_stations_only_S,

                                output       = "count",
                                stationCol            = "Station",
                                speciesCol            = "Species",
                                sessionCol      = "Sessioncol",
                                Xcol                  = "utm_x",
                                Ycol                  = "utm_y",
                                individualCol         = "Individual",
                                recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                occasionLength        = 6,
                                day1                  = "survey",
                                includeEffort         = TRUE,
                                scaleEffort      = FALSE,
                                binaryEffort       = FALSE
)

summary(sdh3)
traps(sdh3)
usage(traps(sdh3))

# with day1 = "station"

sdh3b <- spatialDetectionHistory(recordTableIndividual = recordTableIndividualDingo,
                                species               = "Identified_dingo_subsample",
                                # camOp                 = camop_cam_S,
                                camOp = camop_session2,
                                CTtable               = camtraps_cam_stations_only_S,

                                output       = "count",
                                stationCol            = "Station",
                                speciesCol            = "Species",
                                sessionCol      = "Sessioncol",
                                Xcol                  = "utm_x",
                                Ycol                  = "utm_y",
                                individualCol         = "Individual",
                                recordDateTimeCol     = "DateTimeOriginal",
                                recordDateTimeFormat  = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
                                occasionLength        = 6,

                                day1                  = "station",

                                includeEffort         = TRUE,
                                scaleEffort      = FALSE,
                                binaryEffort       = FALSE
)

summary(sdh3b)
traps(sdh3b)
usage(traps(sdh3b))
